deleteAccount.title: Delete my account
deleteAccount.what: This erases your account and everything that is yours: your passkey sign-in, your photo matches in every event, consents, "Not me" marks, claims and scan records. Event photos themselves stay with the event. This cannot be undone.
deleteAccount.ownerBlocked: You own events. Hand them over to another owner first, then you can delete your account.
deleteAccount.doneText: Your data has been erased from FaceScan. You can start again any time with a new face scan.
deleteAccount.passkeyNote: Your phone may still keep the FaceScan passkey. Remove it in your phone's password manager (Google Password Manager or iCloud Keychain).

help.title: FaceScan help
help.subtitle: Quick answers. Nothing you type leaves your phone.
help.hello: Hi! Pick a question below or type your own.
help.unknown: Sorry, I don't know that one yet. Try one of the questions below, or ask the event organiser.

q.find: How do I find my photos?
q.none: Why don't I see any photos?
q.notMe: A photo is not of me
q.unclear: My face isn't clear in some photos
q.newPhone: How do I sign in on another phone?
q.delete: How do I delete my data?
q.badLink: The event link or QR doesn't work

a.find: Open Scan, agree, look at the camera and blink once. FaceScan then looks for you in every event and shows your photos under My photos.
a.none: The event's photos may still be uploading or processing. Try a new scan later, in good light, without sunglasses or a mask. If nothing comes up, you may not be in this event's photos.
a.notMe: Open the photo, tap More options and choose "This is not me". It disappears at once and FaceScan never shows it to you again.
a.unclear: Use Find more: describe the moment (for example "cake cutting"), tap your face in a photo and take a quick scan to claim it. The organiser may check it first.
a.passkey: A passkey is your phone's fingerprint or face unlock, used instead of a password. No email or password is needed and nobody can guess it.
a.newPhone: If your passkey is saved in your Google or Apple account, tap "I've been here before" on the new phone. If not, start again with a passkey on that phone and scan once more.
a.faceStored: No. The scan is kept in memory only, compared once and thrown away. FaceScan keeps only which photos are yours. You can turn any event off on the Privacy page.
a.delete: Go to Privacy and use "Delete my account": type DELETE to erase your account and everything that is yours. Event photos stay with the event.
a.badLink: Links can expire or be switched off by the organiser. Ask them for a new link or QR code. You can also just scan: FaceScan looks in every open event.

account.privacyText: FaceScan keeps your name, your email (encrypted) and your passkey's public key. Your face scan is checked live and never stored; FaceScan keeps only which event photos are yours, and only you can see them. You can turn off any event or delete your account at any time on the Privacy page.
